root_trace: FirmwareAcceptanceController is exported and tested but has no operator/controller entry point consumed by C3-HARNESS.
The production launcher replaces the environment with a four-variable physical environment that does not establish the executable/runtime allowlist needed to resolve the pinned uv command.
stdout.readline and writes are unbounded, stderr is never drained, and only the post-terminate wait has a deadline.
The proposal claim is a copied string; no ResourceClaims object acquires, owns, retains, or releases it.
Process creation identity is sampled once and not revalidated before termination, exit, reap, or claim release.
create_proposal retains the caller's mutable request by reference and execute never recomputes/canonicalizes it before using the call, allowing post-signature substitution.
The decision verifier is only injected and authorization accepts any truthy delegated_authority string instead of durable exact-path O/C1 artifacts.

The controller writes a parallel controller-calls chain and bypasses AcceptanceBroker.record/admit, so the existing bound-operation, identity, raw-result, ordered-chain, expiry, and cleanup validations do not protect dispatch.

required: Provide one isolated firmware-acceptance controller entry point that C3-HARNESS can invoke without exposing the MCP command, environment, endpoint, or process handle to O or target workers.

Freeze proposal bytes at create-once publication; load and hash-validate a separately authored signed O decision and derived delegated/C1 authorization; reject mutation, substitution, replay, expiry, revocation, or mismatched call identity before launch.
Reuse and, only where necessary, minimally extend AcceptanceBroker.record/admit and canonical bound-operation validation instead of maintaining a weaker parallel evidence chain.
Use a viable scrubbed inherited environment for the exact pinned MCP command while clearing ambient physical capability and preserving only the reviewed lane routing/cache variables.

Use bounded MCP initialization, initialized notification, call/result/error framing, stdout read/write deadlines, concurrent bounded stderr capture, safe cancellation/termination, and exact exit/reap evidence.

Acquire an exact ResourceClaims claim owned by the controller identity before process launch, retain it through verified child exit/reap and cleanup recording, and fail closed on acquisition, identity, cleanup, or release ambiguity.

Add focused host-only regressions for post-signature mutation, durable-artifact mismatch/replay/expiry, no-launch rejection, silent stdout, stderr pressure, crash/timeout/cancel cleanup, identity mismatch, and claim retention/release.
explicit_nonrequirements: Do not add a scheduler, workflow framework, database, broad hardware abstraction, or final target project implementation.
Do not expose physical MCP capability to F.C3.O or target workers.
Do not change coding V1 or legacy schema-less firmware parsing/lifecycle behavior.
Do not modify the generic Codex lane controller if a dedicated firmware control entry point satisfies the boundary with less regression risk.
Do not launch the real MCP server or touch hardware during this repair.
consolidated_smallest_sufficient_repair.cost_benefit: Without these two consolidated boundaries C3 is either blocked or uncertifying and can dispatch a substituted call, hang, or race a board without enforceable ownership. The repair is moderate but isolated and reuses accepted broker, process-identity, and resource-claim primitives; its benefit decisively outweighs its contained complexity and test cost.
